preview.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
preview.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC

messages.subject: HANGS Construction Services Q3 2026 payroll reports
messages.body:
Hello,

Please prepare the Q3 2026 payroll reports for HANGS Construction Services LLC: Form 941, the ESD unemployment insurance tax and wage report, the Paid Leave and WA Cares report, and the L&I workers' compensation quarterly report. Each report is a draft for review; nothing is filed or paid until the review is done.

Attached are the Q3 2026 payroll register, the federal tax deposit log and the Q2 2026 year-to-date wages by employee. The register is the final export from the payroll system for the six Q3 paydays, July 10 to September 18. Every federal tax deposit for the quarter went through EFTPS.

Omar Rasmussen gave payroll a WA Cares exemption approval in July, and payroll stopped that deduction from the July 24 payday.

Tomas Arvelo is paid through accounts payable, not payroll, for concrete finishing at Tideflats Cold Storage.

Two more employees say WA Cares exemption applications have been sent in. No approval letter has arrived for either application, so payroll still takes the WA Cares deduction from both employees' paychecks.

The other records are in the client folder: the employer accounts, the Q1 and Q2 returns as filed, the 2026 rate records, the employee roster, the exemption approvals on file, the payroll ledger accounts and the labor vendors paid.

Dana Whitfield
Controller, HANGS Construction Services LLC
payroll@hangs-gc.example

sources.title: 26 CFR 31.3102-4, Special rules regarding Additional Medicare Tax
sources.issuer: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (eCFR text)

passages.q: Does a married filing status change when Additional Medicare withholding starts?
passages.a: An employer is required to collect from each of its employees the tax imposed by section 3101(b)(2) (Additional Medicare Tax) with respect to wages for employment performed for the employer by the employee only to the extent the employer pays wages to the employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year. This rule applies regardless of the employee's filing status or other income.

passages.q: When is the Q3 2026 Form 941 due?
passages.a: Your Form 941 is due by the last day of the month that follows the end of the quarter. ... 3. July, August, September September 30 October 31 ... If you made timely deposits in full payment of your taxes for the quarter, you may file by the 10th day of the 2nd month that follows the end of the quarter. ... If any due date for filing falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday, you may file your return on the next business day.

passages.q: Which employees are counted on line 1, and what goes on lines 2 and 3?
passages.a: Enter the number of employees on your payroll for the pay period including March 12, June 12, September 12, or December 12, for the quarter indicated at the top of Form 941. ... Enter amounts on line 2 that would also be included in box 1 of your employees’ Forms W-2. ... Enter the federal income tax you withheld (or were required to withhold) from your employees on this quarter’s wages, tips, taxable fringe benefits, and supplemental unemployment compensation benefits.

passages.q: Which wages go on line 5a, and where does Social Security stop for each employee?
passages.a: The social security tax rate is 6.2% each for the employee and employer. The social security wage base limit is $184,500. ... For 2026, the rate of social security tax on taxable wages is 6.2% (0.062) each for the employer and employee. Stop paying social security tax on and entering an employee’s wages on line 5a when the employee’s taxable wages and tips reach $184,500 for the year. ... line 5a (column 1) x 0.124 line 5a (column 2)

passages.q: What goes on Schedule B, and what must it equal?
passages.a: File Schedule B if you’re a semiweekly schedule depositor. You’re a semiweekly schedule depositor if you reported more than $50,000 of employment taxes in the lookback period or accumulated a tax liability of $100,000 or more on any given day in the current or prior calendar year. ... On Schedule B, list your tax liability for each day. Your tax liability is based on the dates wages were paid. ... Your total liability for the quarter must equal line 12 on Form 941.

passages.q: How do 401(k) deferrals and Section 125 premiums change income tax, Social Security and Medicare wages?
passages.a: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable. ... Cafeteria plan benefits under section 125. If employee chooses cash or other taxable benefit, subject to all employment taxes. If employee chooses a nontaxable benefit, the treatment is the same as if the benefit was provided outside the plan.

passages.q: When must Additional Medicare Tax be withheld from a paycheck?
passages.a: In addition to withholding Medicare tax at 1.45%, you must withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax from wages you pay to an employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year. You’re required to begin withholding Additional Medicare Tax in the pay period in which you pay wages in excess of $200,000 to an employee and continue to withhold it each pay period until the end of the calendar year.

passages.q: When was each Q3 deposit due?
passages.a: If you accumulate $100,000 or more in taxes on any day during a monthly or semiweekly deposit period ..., you must deposit the tax by the next business day, whether you’re a monthly or semiweekly schedule depositor. ... A business day is any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. ... The term “legal holiday” means any legal holiday in the District of Columbia. ... July 3—Independence Day (observed) September 7—Labor Day

sources.title: Publication 15-B (2026), Employer's Tax Guide to Fringe Benefits

passages.q: Are the Section 125 health premiums left out of Social Security and Medicare wages as well as income tax wages?
passages.a: A cafeteria plan, including an FSA, provides participants an opportunity to receive qualified benefits on a pre-tax basis. ... Accident and health benefits (but not Archer medical savings accounts (Archer MSAs) or long-term care insurance). ... Accident and health benefits Exempt (except 2% shareholder-employees of S corporations). Exempt Exempt

passages.q: Is Tomas Arvelo, paid by the hour through accounts payable, an employee for Form 941?
passages.a: In determining whether the person providing service is an employee or an independent contractor, all information that provides evidence of the degree of control and independence must be considered. ... The keys are to look at the entire relationship and consider the extent of the right to direct and control the worker. ... If you classify an employee as an independent contractor and you have no reasonable basis for doing so, then you may be held liable for employment taxes for that worker

sources.title: Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026 (90 FR 49047)

passages.q: What is the Social Security Administration's contribution and benefit base for 2026?
passages.a: Cost-of-Living Increase and Other Determinations for 2026 ... The OASDI contribution and benefit base is $184,500 for remuneration paid in 2026 and self-employment income earned in tax years beginning in 2026. The OASDI contribution and benefit base serves as the maximum annual earnings on which OASDI taxes are paid.
